newsitem.title: USA: Clinton thanks jurors, declines comment on decision.
newsitem.headline: Clinton thanks jurors, declines comment on decision.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Friday declined comment on the death sentence passed on Timothy McVeigh for the 1995 bombing of a federal building in Oklahoma City, but thanked the jury for their "deliberations and thoroughness."
"Since there is another trial pending, I cannot comment on the jury's decision," Clinton said in a written statement.

The jury in Denver, Colorado, deliberated for 11 hours before deciding that McVeigh should be executed. They rejected defence pleas to sentence the Gulf War veteran to life in prison or the bombing that killed 168 people.

"But on behalf of all Americans, I thank the jurors for their deliberations and their thoroughness as they made these grave decisions," Clinton said. "This investigation and trial have confirmed our country's faith in its justice system."

Clinton told the victims and their families he knew their healing could be measured "only one day at a time" and said the prayers and support of all Americans would be with them every one of those days.
McVeigh was convicted on June 2 of 11 murder and conspiracy charges in the bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building on April 19, 1995. More than 500 people were also injured in the blast.
